name: Clavicle lengthening osteotomy

card.summary: A rare, extreme surgery floated on forums to widen the shoulders by cutting and lengthening the collarbones; no cosmetic studies found.
card.note: No published trials of the operation for cosmetic shoulder widening were found.

quick.overview:
Clavicle lengthening osteotomy is a surgical idea in which a collarbone is cut and lengthened to widen the shoulders. In looksmaxxing it is described as an extreme, rarely performed hardmaxxing option.

No clinical studies of the operation for appearance were found. Surgical literature on the clavicle mostly covers fractures, non-union and malunion.
quick.mechanism: An osteotomy is a surgical cut through bone. Applied to the clavicle, the goal would be to increase bone length and so shoulder breadth. Related operations in the literature treat painful non-union and malunion after fractures.
quick.risks: Clavicle surgery sits close to nerves and vessels. A published case series of operations for late fracture complications mentions conditions such as thoracic outlet syndrome and brachial plexus neuroma among the problems treated. Anesthesia for clavicle surgery often involves nerve blocks that can affect breathing muscles.

lead: Clavicle lengthening osteotomy refers to a surgical procedure in which the collarbone is cut and lengthened with the aim of widening the shoulders. It appears in looksmaxxing circles as a rare, extreme hardmaxxing option and is not an established cosmetic operation.

No studies or trials of clavicle lengthening for cosmetic shoulder widening were found. The surgical literature on the clavicle concerns fractures and their complications. One case series described operative treatment of late complications of clavicle fractures, including painful non-union, malunion and neurogenic or vascular thoracic outlet syndrome [1].
Registered clinical trials on the clavicle found in the sources are about fracture treatment, plates and pins, not cosmetic lengthening [2][3].
infobox: Wider shoulders by lengthening the clavicle

paras: The clavicle is a long bone that holds the shoulder away from the chest, and males usually have longer clavicles than females [4]. Because bone length sets the skeletal part of shoulder width, some looksmaxxers raise lengthening as a theoretical way to change it. Training cannot change bone length.

Clavicle surgery in the published literature addresses fractures, painful non-union, hypertrophic malunion and related nerve and vascular problems. A 2003 series of 17 patients treated late complications from high-energy clavicle injuries [1]. Anesthesia reports describe regional nerve blocks, including interscalene and cervical plexus blocks, for clavicle surgery, and note that interscalene injection can cause temporary paralysis of one side of the diaphragm [5][6].

No risk data exist for cosmetic lengthening specifically. General risks of clavicle operations in the literature include non-union, nerve injury and thoracic outlet complications, as described in the series above [1].
No studies found. Registered clinical trials on the clavicle concern fracture management [2][3].
